sections.markdown:
## C2 — Vehicle failures, collision avoidance and skid control

FACT_ID: sec14-R01 | anchor: A01
The manual gives stopping, turning or accelerating as possible responses to an impending collision. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec14-R02 | anchor: A01
Read the vehicle’s manual for instructions on its ABS. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec14-R03 | anchor: A01
For a quick stop with working ABS, press the brake firmly as hard as possible and maintain that pressure. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec14-R04 | anchor: A01
ABS operation may push back through the pedal; keep the pedal depressed rather than releasing it. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec14-R05 | anchor: A01
Without ABS, emergency braking should be as firm as possible without locking the wheels. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec14-R06 | anchor: A01
If non-ABS brakes lock and the vehicle skids, promptly release the brake pedal. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec14-R07 | anchor: A01
After that non-ABS skid stops, reapply the brakes and repeat as necessary until stopped. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec14-R08 | anchor: A01
The manual says a vehicle can usually turn sooner than it can stop and suggests considering an evasive turn. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec14-R09 | anchor: A01
For an evasive turn, hold the wheel with both hands and prepare to maintain control after turning or changing lanes. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec14-R10 | anchor: A01
Steer toward the path you want the vehicle to follow. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec14-R11 | anchor: A01
The source describes ABS as allowing steering during braking without skidding when a turn and slowdown or stop are needed. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec14-R12 | anchor: A01
For a quick turn without ABS, the source sequence is brake, release the pedal, then steer. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec14-R13 | anchor: A01
That non-ABS guidance warns against locking the front wheels or turning so sharply that the vehicle plows straight ahead. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec14-R14 | anchor: A01
Acceleration may avoid a threatened side or rear impact when space ahead provides an escape. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec14-R15 | anchor: A01
After accelerating out of a collision threat, reduce speed when the danger passes. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec14-R16 | anchor: A02
Wetness, snow or ice can make an otherwise safe road hazardous; high speed increases skid risk during a sudden turn or stop. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec14-R17 | anchor: A02
A skid occurs when the tires lose their grip on the roadway. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec14-R18 | anchor: A02
For a skid already underway, the source instructs staying off the brake until the vehicle slows, warning that braking can worsen it. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec14-R19 | anchor: A02
During a skid, steer toward the desired travel direction; as the vehicle straightens, correct the wheel back to avoid a skid the other way. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec14-R20 | anchor: A02
Keep correcting the steering until controlled forward travel is restored. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec14-R21 | anchor: A02
Lap-and-shoulder restraints are the manual’s main protection against injury when a collision cannot be avoided. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec14-R22 | anchor: A02
For a rear impact, the handbook directs bracing against the seat back with the head against its restraint. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec14-R23 | anchor: A02
After a rear impact, prepare to brake so your vehicle is not pushed into another vehicle. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec14-R24 | anchor: A02
In a side impact, lap-and-shoulder belts help keep the driver at the controls; prepare to steer or brake to avoid another collision. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec14-R25 | anchor: A02
For an unavoidable threatened frontal impact, the manual suggests turning in an attempt to avoid impact or receive a glancing rather than direct head-on blow. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec14-R26 | anchor: A02
The frontal-impact passage describes an equipped airbag inflating and then deflating, and calls for readiness to avoid a subsequent impact. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec14-R27 | anchor: A02
Keep lap-and-shoulder belts in use to remain behind the wheel and gain protection during a possible second collision. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0036]

verification_debt.claim_text: Pages35–36 ABS/non-ABS, evasive-turn and skid procedures need current manufacturer/issuer review. Broad source claims about stopping/turning without skidding and brakes not working during a skid are not vehicle-independent guarantees. Do not conflate failure pumping, non-ABS lockup release and working-ABS sustained pressure.

Page36 bracing/evasive impact and airbag statements require current crash-safety/vehicle-specific review. The source says an equipped airbag will inflate, but deployment depends on circumstances; no guaranteed deployment or universal collision maneuver is accepted.
Page36 skid/steering illustration content has not been rendered or interpreted. Text sequences remain distinct; diagram direction/geometry is not inferred.
